title: Mycelium: A Meta-Study of Hallucination Detection Across Provenance, Typology, and Granularities
abstract: arXiv:2610.33608v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Hallucination detection is increasingly important for evaluating and deploying large language models. However, existing methods are often compared across benchmarks that define and measure hallucination in substantially different ways, making reported scores difficult to interpret across settings. We study hallucination detection as a benchmark-conditioned measurement problem and organize existing benchmarks along three axes: provenance, which describes how model outputs and evidence conditions are obtained; typology, which captures the factuality and faithfulness failures represented by benchmark labels; and granularity, which specifies the unit at which hallucinations are annotated, predicted, and evaluated. Using this framework, we analyze how benchmark construction, annotation, and evaluation choices shape the underlying prediction task, and relate detector mechanisms and assumptions to the settings in which their performance is me

translated_title: Mycelium：面向来源、类型学与粒度的幻觉检测元研究
translated_abstract: 幻觉检测对于大型语言模型的评估与部署正变得日益重要。然而，现有方法通常是在以截然不同的方式定义和衡量幻觉的各类基准上进行比较的，这使得所报告的分数难以在不同设置之间进行解读。我们将幻觉检测视为一个以基准为条件的测量问题来研究，并沿三个维度对现有基准进行组织：来源，它描述模型输出和证据条件是如何获得的；类型学，它刻画基准标签所代表的事实性与忠实性失败；粒度，它规定了幻觉被标注、预测和评估的单元。利用这一框架，我们分析了基准构建、标注和评估选择如何塑造底层预测任务，并将检测器的机制与假设和其性能被评测的具体设置联系起来。
tldr: 该论文将幻觉检测视为以基准为条件的测量问题，提出从来源、类型学和粒度三个维度对现有基准进行组织与元分析，揭示基准构建与评估选择如何影响幻觉检测任务本身及检测器性能的可比性。
en_tdlr: This meta-study frames hallucination detection as a benchmark-conditioned measurement problem, organizing existing benchmarks along provenance, typology, and granularity axes to show how benchmark construction and evaluation choices shape the underlying prediction task and detector performance.
